channel.title: The Grant Desk - Grants, AI, Tech & Research, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Grants, AI, Tech & Research, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Jane Street Graduate Research Fellowship 2027 (tuition plus USD 50,000 stipend) (closes 13 Nov)
item.description:
Jane Street
Deadline: 13 Nov 2026
Award: Full tuition and fees for the award year plus a USD 50,000 stipend (or local-currency equivalent; taxable). Finalists receive USD 5,000. No application fee.

Jane Street's Graduate Research Fellowship supports exceptional doctoral students in electrical engineering and computer science, mathematics, physics or statistics; research does not need to relate to trading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network (AIAI): Seed Grants 2026 for humanities-forward AI research in Atlanta (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network (AIAI), Mellon Foundation funded
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026
Award: Up to USD 5,000 per project. In line with Mellon policy, no institutional overhead may be charged. Individuals taking the award outside an institution or employer pay income tax on it. No application fee.

AIAI funds humanities-forward AI research and community building that takes place in, or is focused on, the city of Atlanta. 2026 RESEARCH AREAS: Data Centers; AI Civics; AI Literacies; AI and Archives; Small Language Models; Capitalism, Anticapitalism, and Critique.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Democracy Foundation: Democracy Residency 'European Dream' 2027 (Kuldiga, Latvia; Liepaja European Capital of Culture) (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
Democracy Foundation (Kuldiga), part of the Liepaja 2027 European Capital of Culture programme
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026
Award: EUR 1,000 stipend per participant (covering expenses during the residency, including travel), plus up to EUR 1,000 per participant to develop and run their activity, and accommodation in Kuldiga's Old Town. Six participants. No application fee stated.

International interdisciplinary residency run by the Democracy Foundation in Kuldiga, Latvia, as part of the Liepaja 2027 European Capital of Culture programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Digital Democracy Edinburgh 2027: Call for Proposals (TICTeC, mySociety, AI4CI, Scottish Government) (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
mySociety (TICTeC) with the AI for Collective Intelligence (AI4CI) Hub, the Scottish Government and the Edinburgh Futures Institute, University of Edinburgh
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: NO GUARANTEED CASH, listed as an exception at the editor's request: accepted speakers get complimentary conference registration, and a limited number of travel scholarships are available for speakers who could otherwise not attend (priority to applicants from ODA-eligible countries and under-29s; amount not published). Free to submit.

Digital Democracy Edinburgh is a two-day conference from mySociety's TICTeC (The Impacts of Civic Technology) series, run with the AI for Collective Intelligence (AI4CI) Research Hub, the Scottish Government and the Edinburgh Futures Institute, for researchers, policy makers and practitioners...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Connected Canvas: The National Gallery Digital Commission 2027 (emerging UK creatives) (closes 17 Nov)
item.description:
National Gallery (National Gallery X), London
Deadline: 17 Nov 2026, 23:59 GMT
Award: GBP 15,000 commission. Up to 10 shortlisted applicants receive GBP 500 each to develop proposals.

National Gallery X commissions a new digital, generative, screen-based or sound work for its three-screen LED canvas in the gallery. Open to UK-based emerging creatives in their first five years of practice who are not in full-time education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Van Alen Institute: Re:Paris Prize, USD 35,000 travel research fellowship on design in Africa and its diaspora (US-based applicants) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Van Alen Institute
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026
Award: USD 35,000 travel fellowship; one US-based winner selected through this open call (two Africa-based winners were selected via the 2026 Pan-African Biennale).

The Re:Paris Prize, run by Van Alen Institute, funds research into how design plays a transformative role in Africa and its diaspora. Each winner receives a USD 35,000 travel fellowship for field research that requires international travel to connect with experts and opportunities.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Cities Deliver: AI Solutions for Public Services (Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation, USD 500,000 to 2 million) (closes 29 Nov)
item.description:
The Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation, managed by RF Catalytic Capital (RFCC)
Deadline: 29 Nov 2026
Award: USD 50 million total. Seed track USD 500,000 to under 1 million; Scale track USD 1 to 2 million. 24-month grants, 50 percent at start and 50 percent on a documented mid-term milestone. No application fee stated.

A USD 50 million open call from the Rockefeller Foundation and OpenAI Foundation for organisations working with city governments to improve public services through AI, especially for underserved communities.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme 2027/28 (HKD 344,400 a year for up to three years; 400 fellowships, practice-led art PhDs included) (closes 1 Dec)
item.description:
Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong, with eight Hong Kong universities
Deadline: 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 Hong Kong time
Award: Annual stipend of HKD 344,400 (about USD 44,150) plus a conference and research travel allowance of HKD 14,400 a year, for up to three years (2026/27 rates as published by the RGC). Some universities add top-ups: HKBU lists a HKD 40,000-a-year Elite Scholar Award for three years, a further HKD 20,000 travel top-up, four years of tuition waiver and two years of guaranteed accommodation. 400 fellowships for 2027/28.

The Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, run by the Research Grants Council, funds around 400 new full-time PhD students a year at eight Hong Kong universities, in any discipline, including AI, computing and data science programmes and practice-led art research (Hong Kong Baptist University's Academy...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IHS AI and the Workforce Research Grants (up to USD 20,000) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Institute for Humane Studies (IHS)
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Up to USD 20,000 per award; larger awards possible for exceptional projects. Covers research costs (research assistants, datasets, LLM subscriptions, travel to present), not salary or overhead.

Research grants for academic scholars studying how AI is changing jobs, productivity and economic opportunity. Economics-leaning; IHS is a libertarian-leaning institute. Funds direct research costs only. No country restriction stated. Deadline 15 December 2026 (no time zone given).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie: Open Call Cultural Education and Digital Technology 2026 (closes 16 Dec)
item.description:
Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie (with LKCA and DEN)
Deadline: 16 Dec 2026, 15:00 CET
Award: EUR 10,000 to EUR 25,000 per project, up to 100% of total project costs (no co-funding required). Total budget EUR 500,000.

Open call (Open Oproep Cultuureducatie en Digitale Technologie) for cultural education projects in which children and young people work creatively with digital technology. Run by the Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie with LKCA and DEN.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IJ4EU Freelancer Support Scheme 2026-27, Second Call (cross-border teams of freelance journalists) (closes 2 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU): International Press Institute and European Journalism Centre
Deadline: 2 Feb 2027
Award: Up to EUR 20,000 per team, plus training and mentoring.

A strand of IJ4EU for freelance journalists: teams of at least two freelancers in two eligible countries receive funding, training and mentoring for a cross-border investigation.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IJ4EU Investigation Support Scheme 2026-27, Second Call (cross-border investigative journalism) (closes 2 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Investigative Journalism for Europe (IJ4EU): International Press Institute and European Journalism Centre
Deadline: 2 Feb 2027
Award: EUR 5,000 to 50,000 per project, from a EUR 1.2 million pot.

IJ4EU funds cross-border investigative journalism in the public interest, by teams of journalists and newsrooms working across at least two eligible countries. Eligibility is by country of residence, not citizenship; applications are in English.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Horizon Europe Cluster 2 2027: Open Topic on Reinvigorating and Shielding European Democracy (DEMOCRACY-09, two-stage) (closes 4 May 2027)
item.description:
European Research Executive Agency (REA) / European Commission, Horizon Europe
Deadline: 4 May 2027
Award: EUR 2.0 to 3.7 million per project; EUR 22 million indicative topic budget. Research and Innovation Action.

Two-stage open topic in the Horizon Europe Cluster 2 call 'Culture, Creativity and Inclusive Society - 2027 - Two-stage' (HORIZON-CL2-2027-02-DEMOCRACY-09-two-stage). Opens 2 March 2027; first-stage deadline 4 May 2027 (short proposal), with invited full proposals in a second stage.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Horizon Europe Cluster 2 2027: AI, Deepfakes and Democracy (DEMOCRACY-04) and The Role of Private Companies in Democracy (DEMOCRACY-07) (closes 23 Sep 2027)
item.description:
European Research Executive Agency (REA) / European Commission, Horizon Europe
Deadline: 23 Sep 2027
Award: DEMOCRACY-04: EUR 3.5 to 4.0 million per project, EUR 20 million indicative topic budget. DEMOCRACY-07: EUR 3.5 to 4.0 million per project, EUR 8 million indicative topic budget. Lump-sum Research and Innovation Actions.

Two 2027 topics in the Horizon Europe Cluster 2 call 'Culture, Creativity and Inclusive Society - 2027' (opens 13 May 2027, deadline 23 September 2027), both Research and Innovation Actions with lump-sum funding.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: BlueDot Impact: Seed Grants for new AI safety and biosecurity projects (USD 20,000 to 200,000, rolling)
item.description:
BlueDot Impact
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: USD 20,000 to 200,000 for 6 to 12 months (requests under USD 20,000 go to BlueDot Rapid Grants). No application fee.

BlueDot Impact's Seed Grants fund the first 6 to 12 months of a new AI safety or biosecurity project or organisation, covering founders' living costs, compute, tools and running costs, and travel. WHAT YOU GET: USD 20,000 to 200,000 (smaller requests go to Rapid Grants).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Outrider AI + Nuclear Reporting Fund (rolling)
item.description:
Outrider Foundation
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Up to USD 10,000 per reporting project.

Outrider funds journalists and outlets reporting on the intersection of artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons: how AI is changing nuclear risk, command and control, and policy. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis through the Google Form linked from the fund page. No application fee.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Pantheon: Research Fellowship in robot learning (remote, USD 6,000/month) (rolling)
item.description:
Pantheon
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: USD 6,000 per month stipend (about USD 12,000 to 18,000 over the fellowship) plus enterprise-level compute for experiments. No application fee.

Pantheon, which builds general-purpose robot models, runs a remote research fellowship in which each fellow leads a project on an open problem the team meets while training and evaluating its models; strong results are folded into the next generation of those models.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: BRAID Creative Commissions 2027: A Promise in Return (Responsible AI, GBP 8,000-12,000, Edinburgh Art Festival)
item.description: BRAID (Bridging Responsible AI Divides), University of Edinburgh, with Inspace, the Institute for Design Informatics and the Edinburgh Futures Institute · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · Around seven commissions with budgets of GBP 8,000 to 12,000 each, inclusive of VAT and all costs. No application fee.

item.title: ART4MENTAL open call for artists: VR content for mental-health support (EUR 5,000 sub-grants)
item.description: ART4MENTAL (Creative Europe project) · deadline 11 Nov 2026 · Sub-grant of up to EUR 5,000 per artist for 20 selected artists (EUR 100,000 pool), plus VR training, mentorship, a residency in the Ukrainian Carpathians and exhibition opportunities. No application fee.

item.title: Zoud GameLab 2026: Global Game Jam financial-literacy jam (prize and funding pool up to USD 140,000)
item.description: Zoud (UAE National Financial Wellbeing and Sustainability Initiative) with Global Game Jam · deadline 15 Nov 2026 · Shared prize and development-support funding pool of up to USD 140,000 across best overall game, runner-up, third place, financial-literacy impact, regional perspective, compelling gameplay and a Best Game from the UAE award; individual prize amounts are not published. No entry fee.

item.title: City of Palo Alto Code:ART 2027: Interactive Media Installations (up to USD 9,000 each)
item.description: City of Palo Alto Public Art Program · deadline 16 Nov 2026 · Up to USD 9,000 per installation, for up to five installations. No application fee.

item.title: City of Palo Alto Code:ART 2027: Lytton Plaza Installation Commission (USD 20,000)
item.description: City of Palo Alto Public Art Program · deadline 16 Nov 2026 · USD 20,000 commission budget. No application fee.

item.title: MIT Solve: 2027 Global Challenges
item.description: MIT Solve (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) · deadline 02 Nov 2026 · Every selected Solver team receives a USD 10,000 grant funded by Solve, plus access to a pool of over USD 1 million in prize funding at selection and additional funding opportunities throughout the program. Sponsor prizes range from USD 100,000 to 200,000, including the AI for Humanity Prize (up to USD 150,000, Patrick J. McGovern Foundation), the Collegium Prize for Innovation (USD 100,000), the Citizens Workforce Innovation Prize (USD 100,000), the Crescent Enterprises AI for Social Innovation Prize (USD 100,000) and the Seeding the Future Prize (USD 150,000). No application fee.

item.title: GAIN SSA: AI Safety Essentials Fellowship (inaugural cohort)
item.description: GAIN SSA (Global AI Youth Network, Sub-Saharan Africa) · deadline 08 Nov 2026 · Micro-grant pool funding top capstone proposals at USD 500 to 1,000 each (capped at USD 1,000), usable for compute access, communication work such as Substack Pro subscriptions for writers, or travel to AI alignment conferences in Sub-Saharan Africa. The fellowship itself is free to attend (no participation fee, no application fee); no stipend is paid during the program.

item.title: Creative Industries Fund NL: Residency Videotage 2027 (Hong Kong)
item.description: Creative Industries Fund NL (Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie), with Videotage · deadline 21 Oct 2026 · One residency grant: EUR 5,000 for a two-month work period or EUR 6,500 for three months, covering travel, insurance, living expenses, compensation for time invested, and material and transport costs. Housing, work space, Videotage guidance and production costs are paid by the Fund directly to Videotage on top of the grant; accommodation is arranged by Videotage. No application fee.

item.title: OASis Bom Dia Residency 2027 at Cultivamos Cultura (Sao Luis, Portugal)
item.description: Cultivamos Cultura (European OASis project) · deadline 30 Oct 2026 · EUR 1,300 project fee, travel budget up to EUR 500, production and material expenses up to EUR 1,600 (pre-approved), food per diem, plus free accommodation in a private room in a shared farmhouse and access to a workspace or studio and all Cultivamos Cultura spaces and resources.

item.title: Screen Australia Future Leaders Delegation: BitSummit 2027 (Kyoto)
item.description: Screen Australia · deadline 05 Nov 2026 · AUD 6,000 per delegate towards flights, accommodation, event tickets, ground transportation and meals, plus covered travel costs for the pre-departure workshop and the opportunity to exhibit a game on the Australia stand. Up to eight delegates.

item.title: make-a-thek: Mobility Scheme & Knowledge Exchange Programme (Europe + pilot countries)
item.description: make-a-thek (coordinated by Fab Lab Barcelona at IAAC, funded by Horizon Europe) · deadline 01 Dec 2026 · Mobility Scheme: EUR 1,000 flat stipend for experienced practitioners. Knowledge Exchange Programme: EUR 850 flat stipend. Up to 12 participants per track annually. No application fee.

item.title: EU CERV: European Remembrance 2026-27 (CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM)
item.description: European Commission / EACEA (Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme) · deadline 24 Feb 2027 · EUR 50,000 to EUR 500,000 per project, from an estimated call budget of EUR 28 million (EUR 14M Holocaust remembrance of Jewish victims; EUR 5M genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity incl. Roma and LGBTIQ+ victims; EUR 5M colonialism, slavery and migration; EUR 4M democratic transitions). No application fee.
